command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
review="$reports/review-specs.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-specs stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: R1 rests on a claim the code contradicts. Its Problem says returnToNow goes through dispatchAndAnnounce 'so a Now that is not really disabled would announce the date'. But dispatchAndAnnounce announces only when the state changed (`if (outcome.ok && store.getSnapshot() !== stateBefore)`, packages/client/src/controller/useReferenceMoment.ts:80), and RESET_TO_NOW on a live moment returns the same state (`if (state.reference.mode === ReferenceMode.LIVE) return { ok: true, state };`, packages/client/src/model/reduceReferenceMoment.ts:91), which model/referenceMomentPicking.test.ts:91 'should return the same state when resetting a live moment' already tests. So 'nothing is announced' is already guaranteed and tested in the model even without native disabled. The Impact (a 'later regression slipping through') is speculative, and the Fix (a new Gherkin line plus a new unit step reading the live region) adds work for a rule the code already enforces, with a Fix risk of 'low' that ignores this existing guard. Drop R1, or rewrite it to cite useReferenceMoment.ts:80 and reduceReferenceMoment.ts:91 and lower its stake.
